plain: Two Air Force security guards who say they were abducted in 1977 near nuclear missile sites at Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota, both remember the same words: "Do not fear." Michels tells it in his own words, about the guards Mario Woods and Michael Johnson. In one episode he frames the memory as coming out under hypnosis: "Two men, two rooms, hours apart, neither in earshot of the other. The same three words." In another he says simply that they heard the words "over and over again" before the abduction. The written record is a 2017 article by the researcher Robert Hastings, which carries an account Woods wrote for him. In it Woods recalls "voices in my head, more than one, saying, 'Do not fear', over and over." He also says that two weeks after that night, his partner told him he "had heard voices, many voices, saying not to be afraid." At the time of writing, Hastings had only "arranged for hypnotic regression sessions," meaning hypnosis used to try to bring back forgotten memories. So in the 2017 text, both men already hold the shared words in their waking memory from 1977, before any hypnosis, and the article does not report what the sessions later turned up. If the match is real, two men remembered the same message on their own, which would point to a shared experience.

discussion.by: Former USAF Missile Security Policeman Tells of Apparent UFO Abduction at ICBM Site
discussion.text: In the account Woods wrote for Hastings in 2017, before any regression, both men already remember the words: Woods recalls voices saying "‘Do not fear’, over and over", and two weeks after the night his partner tells him he "had heard voices, many voices, saying not to be afraid"; Hastings has only "arranged for hypnotic regression sessions". The tellings place the shared words under hypnosis; the 2017 text has them in both men's waking memory from 1977.
